rendered: According to the review, prodigiosin production is strongly temperature-dependent. It peaks at 25–28 ◦C[1], and it is suppressed at ≥37 ◦C[2]. The figure is consistent with this: Fig. 2[3] shows strongly pigmented, red/pink colonies at the lower temperature and pale cream colonies with no visible red pigment at the higher temperature. The temperature effect is linked to decreased expression and stability of the PigF and PigN enzymes at higher temperatures.[4][5]
